participants: Andrew Musial (closer; recorded under the Fathom speaker label 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)')
summary: Month-end meeting with two days left. Pipeline review first: Andrew is $800 short of $50K, Richard is well short and is chasing three deposits, and Kim reports 20 sets and a 75% show rate. The manager sets the collection rule for the remaining days — deposits do not count toward the target and a client must pay at least $1,200. Once the setter leaves, the whole second half is an open-wallet role-play. Andrew runs it and is coached on the three elements that must be present: state that there are no set payment plans, reassure the prospect you will not put them in financial hardship, and get explicit permission to discuss finances. The manager then demonstrates the full play against Richard, working through monthly surplus, credit cards, available credit, credit score, crypto, gold and home equity, and recommends a $4,000 card payment plus a $2,000 instalment plan. It ends with Richard asking for performance feedback and being given the 25% live-to-call close-rate KPI.
notable: Collection rule stated for the last two days of the month: 'it can't be deposits, so they need to at least give you $1,200. Deposits don't count.' Andrew needs $800 to unlock a $500 bonus.

A prospect with minus $67 in his bank account and a credit score of 'four or five hundred' was taken through an open wallet and remains on the follow-up list, with a Thursday call booked for when 'he gets some money transferred for deposit, and then the 1200 would only be collected.' The manager did caution: 'Be careful with a guy who has negative $67 in his bank account on making payments.'

The scripted open-wallet line is that no set payment plans exist — 'we don't really have any set payment plans. We do everything custom' — while the manager in the same role-play produces standard structures: $1,200 a month for six months, or $4,000 on a credit card plus a $2,000 instalment plan.

Manager's stated affordability guardrail, which is genuinely responsible and should be recorded alongside the rest: 'I try not to take more than 50% to 55% of what they're at the end of each month', 'I don't want to put you in a spot like that. That just doesn't make any sense. It's just not fair to you', and 'I tell them straight up, like, dude, I don't think you should do this.'

In the same role-play the manager probed home equity as a funding source and told the rep that clients have taken equity loans to pay: 'I've had people do it where they'll take equity out on their house, like a little loan or something. You just have to go to the bank and you can do it.' He immediately added he would not recommend it.

When the role-play prospect said he does not take loans for a stated family reason, the manager coached past it: 'Do you think that the people that own those buildings paid for them in cash?... maybe your father made some decisions that didn't work out with credit. Well, that doesn't necessarily mean that credit and loans are bad.'

The 'love it or leave it' trial improvised on the 06/24 Jean-Philippe Rifaat call is now in live use as a standard tool: 'we decided on the Love It or Leave It, because he wanted to, like, he wanted to speak to Trevor first, and I was like, no. That's not possible.'
A prospect's request to speak to Trevor before committing $6,000 was refused outright.

A euro-based prospect who has already paid a deposit may have had the price stated in the wrong currency: 'he was in Euros. So I was like, ah, it's 6k US dollars, it's that's Euros, I shouldn't even have done it, I should have just been like, it's 5.2k Euros.'

Reps are running recorded prospect calls through personal AI assistants: 'after every call, I also run the call through my custom cloud.' The 06/24 1-1 shows the same practice with internal transcripts.
Prospect financial details are written into CRM free-text: 'you just write a note and say this person had negative $67 in their bank account.'
Performance standards stated: the KPI is a 25% live-to-call close rate, there is a separate 'call to commitment' metric that counts deposits, and the manager says Andrew is already at that level.
